newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers try to pre-empt ethanol tax vote.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers try to pre-empt ethanol tax vote.

text.p: Defenders of the fuel-tax exemption for ethanol in the U.S. House sent a letter to House leaders with 100 signatures, including 11 from the key Ways and Means Committee, intended as a pre-emptive move to retain the tax break.

"Right now, we've got the votes," said Representative Jim Nussle, Iowa Republican, co-chair of the Alcohol Fuels Caucus. "We believe we're going to have strong showing in Ways and Means and on the floor."
Backers sent their letter to Gingrich and House Minority Leader Richard Gephardt, Missouri Democrat.
Ways and Means chairman Bill Archer, Texas Republican, is a foe of the ethanol exemption. He was foiled the past two years when he attacked it but has targeted it again this year.

House Speaker Newt Gingrich, Georgia Republican, shielded ethanol from attack in the past. This year, Nussle said, Gingrich has said he would let the Ways and Means Committee make up its mind about the matter.
With that in mind, Nussle said, ethanol backers decided on a "full frontal assault" with a show of strength.
Signers ncluded John Boehner of Ohio, No. 4 in Republican leadership, Judiciary chairman Henry Hyde, Illinois Republican, and Agriculture chairman Bob Smith, Oregon Republican.
Representative David Bonior of Michigan, No 2 in Democratic leadership, signed the letter as well.
Four dozen Republicans signed the letter out of 227 in the House. Nussle said it was a large enough bloc to sway the outcome of bill-drafting.
